text:
ash: heads up — seeing a spike of apiserver 5xx and etcd read/write errors in us-east1 after a NIC regen window on the gpu pool. controller-manager restarted a few times.

maria: +1, dashboards show etcd follower catches and leader elections around the same time. KV write latency jumps to ~200ms.

devon: logs from one etcd pod: `grpc: the connection is unavailable` repeated. attaching short snippet:```time="07:12:02" level=error msg="failed to commit: context deadline exceeded"```

li: seeing kube-proxy conntrack churn on the node side too, lots of TCP resets — could be ip rebind during NIC regen.

ash: confirmed — network team did a rolling NIC firmware push across the cluster's GPU nodes starting ~07:10 UTC. They said it was non-disruptive but maybe connections were flapping.

infra-bot: monitoring alert: etcd_high_commit_latency (3 alerts) · apiserver_5xx_rate (2 alerts) — incident created #INC-2026-431.

sara: is Dedicated GPU provisioning affected? any customer impact on inference endpoints?

maria: yes, a few scheduled Dedicated allocs hit controller-manager errors and stuck in Pending for ~2m then succeeded. Some live hosted API requests saw transient 503s (retry layer caught most).

devon: short-term mitigation idea: throttle NIC regen window+pause on control-plane-affecting hosts; increase etcd client timeouts and bump leader-election retry backoff on controller-manager until we finish rolling.

ash: agreed. @networking — can you pause the rest of the NIC reboots for the region?

li: reached out to networking on call — they paused; halting rollout now.

maria: I've opened a quick patch to bump the etcd client timeout from 10s -> 30s and leader-election leaseRenewDeadline from 15s -> 45s for controller-manager. Pushing to canary first.

ash: nice. also let's drain the worst-hit controlplane nodes one by one and cordon any gpu nodes still in the regen window.

devon: testing the patch in staging now; replicated the gRPC disconnect pattern by dropping conn; increased timeouts prevent immediate failover.

li: FYI we observed a small subset of Pods lost existing connections due to node IP rebind — kubelet is re-registering with new IP quickly but conntrack entries linger and cause half-open issues.

sara: do we need to move high-priority customers to another region? That has cost/latency impacts.

maria: not yet — most traffic recovered after pause + controller-manager patch. If the pause doesn't stabilize in 10m we should plan a partial traffic shift for key Dedicated customers.

ash: can someone update the incident doc with customer impact matrix and potential Runbook steps for NIC regen? Add rollback procedure for the firmware job.

devon: adding notes now. Also filing a follow-up to make NIC regen cohort smaller and add pre-checks for controlplane TCP health.

li: after digging, root cause is likely simultaneous ephemeral IP rebind events + tight etcd/ctrlmgr timeouts. We should adjust orchestration so NIC reboots avoid nodes participating in control plane watch-heavy periods.

maria: agreed — long-term: (1) avoid rolling NIC changes during peak watch/commit windows, (2) make controlplane more tolerant to transient gRPC disconnects, (3) add health gating in the NIC rollout job.

ash: assigning remediation: @devon to land the timeout canary, @li to coordinate with networking on rollout gating, @maria to own incident doc and customer comms.

infra-bot: incident status: mitigation in progress · responders assigned (devon, li, maria) · priority P2.

sara: flagging cost note: if we start region-failover for Dedicated customers, estimate ~35% uplift for mirrored capacity + cross-region egress. Need approval from finance for anything >$10k/day.

maria: noted — we'll avoid failover unless strictly necessary.

ash: update in 8m or sooner if things degrade. thanks all. :thumbsup:

li: update 07:18 UTC — pause holding, canary patch good, apiserver 5xx rate down to baseline, leader elections stopped. Keeping watch for 30m.

maria: incident doc link: https://redwoodinc.share/INC-2026-431 (internal) — adding timeline and next steps for postmortem.

ash: closing thread for now, will reopen if alerts reappear.
